description: The 2025 Legislative Session is underway! This is the first of my weekly newsletters for the 2025 Legislative Session. Because I'm in committee four days a week this Session, I'm planning to get these newsletters out on Thursdays from now on. In next week's newsletter I will talk about ICE enforcement, immigration, some of the tough stuff, as well as a list of all bills I am involved with this year. If you have any ideas you want me to hear, or need help navigating state resources, please email me or call my office: E: Chad.Clifford.House@coleg.gov P: 303-866-5510 What to look forward to this Session: Since last May I have heard from many of you about what is most important to advocate for at the State Capitol. Thank you to those of you reading this who have taken the time to invite me into your spaces -- I am truly grateful to be in this Session with so much engagement from HD37. Below are the legislative priorities I am entering this Session with: Housing: Another year another newsletter, you would likely guess from past newsletters that Housing is what I’m starting off with... One piece of legislation that I am working hard to pass to address our housing problem is something I spoke about at length last session -- construction defects. This must get this passed; giving alternate pathways to resolve construction defect claims besides only litigation is crucial for us to be able to build condominiums and ownable dense housing. The average home price in HD37 is about $700,000. For anyone looking to enter the housing market, or re-enter the housing market to downsize, there is virtually no housing at an "affordable" (pretend affordable is a $350k) level. One of many steps needed to combat this is to allow for alternative resolutions to resolving construction defects. It really has to be the foundation to start building middle-income housing, and if not addressed House District 37 is going to lose young people, families, and likely impact our workforce. Public Safety: As the only sworn Peace Officer in the General Assembly, my voice in the law enforcement space is often useful. I've spent every Thursday for the last eight months Co Chairing a Legislative Law Enforcement Working Group, and out of it have come four Topic Groups. Of these groups, so far two bills have been introduced, HB25-1031 Law Enforcement Whistleblower Protection, and HB25-1136 Peace Officer Conduct Database. Both of these bills protect the Peace Officers who protect us. There will be a lot more conversation about these bills to come as they move through the process. Another important aspect of public safety I'm engaged in is the implementation of Proposition 130, which even though it was on your ballot in November and passed with 52.79% of the vote, it still requires statute and some structures created to be implemented. Prop 130 allocates $350 Million in state general funds to county and municipal law enforcement for training, recruitment, and retention as well as a $1 Million in death benefits to certain first responders who die in the line of duty. There are some sticking points that myself and many members of the legislature want to make sure are properly addressed, and I anticipate that the final implementation language may take us all session to work out - and we all expect this to be implemented and funding started this year. Accessibility: One of my bills every year is dedicated to the disability community's wants and needs. This year, they approached me with the idea to codify the 1999 Olmstead v. L.C. decision. HB25-1017, Community Integration Plan Individuals with Disabilities. This states that the government cannot institutionalize people with disabilities without justification, and furthermore must do its best to integrate those with disabilities into society. It emphasizes community-based living, supports employment, education, and healthcare, and fosters collaboration among state agencies, service providers, and local communities to enhance the quality of life for individuals with disabilities. Airport: While I have no knowledge of legislation coming through addressing airports, I do see it as my responsibility to bridge the concerns of the community and of the airport industry. This should be an ongoing dialogue, and I will create and support spaces with the airport and community groups that support communication. Healthcare: I have heard from a number of constituents who have had problems with the state's Medicaid program. 29% of HD37 residents are on Health First Colorado, and I am looking for ways to make the process easier. There is often overlap with federal regulation that makes some areas more difficult. Another issue that has been brought to my attention is the reality that there exist harmful elder care facilities and problems in the state with oversight over these facilities. I am working to address this problem with our state agencies. In addition to all of the bills I'm working on, this year I'm serving in the Judiciary Committee and the State, Civic, Military, & Veterans Affairs Committee. I was also this week appointed to the Enforcement Community Services Grant Program Committee and the Legislative Oversight Committee Concerning Colorado Jail Standards. Last, if you ever want to come by the Capitol my staff would love to accommodate that -- just reach out! The best contact is my Legislative Aide's: chris@chadforcolorado.com or my own: chad@chadforcolorado.com .
